blocks.text:
**Programme year:** 2026  

This trip combines flights, road transfers, river journeys, a catamaran, canoes and several different types of accommodation. In the cities, you explore colonial history and local culture; beyond them, most of your time is spent among forests, rivers, islands and waterfalls, watching for wildlife. The route involves frequent changes of location, allowing you to see several very different parts of the region in 14 days.

Guyana gives the journey its most dramatic introduction to nature: after Georgetown, you fly over unbroken rainforest to Kaieteur, then leave the country that same evening. The pace changes in Suriname. Here, Paramaribo's wooden architecture, old coffee plantations and Maroon villages sit alongside long river journeys into the interior. Suriname hosts most of the jungle programme.

French Guiana offers another contrast. After crossing the Marowijne border river, you travel through Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni and Cayenne to Kourou. The history of the penal colony meets a modern space centre, while a boat trip takes you to Île Royale and Île Saint-Joseph. The journey then returns to Suriname and heads far from the cities, to the Upper Suriname River and Kabalebo.

This route suits travellers interested in both well-known sights and an unusual combination of cultures and natural environments. In Paramaribo, a basilica, mosque and synagogue stand close together; on the Upper Suriname River, you meet Maroon communities; and in French Guiana, European infrastructure sits beside a tropical coast. Languages, borders, transport and the character of each day change throughout the trip.
